verses.text: "Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground with no throne, daughter of the Babylonians. You will no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take the millstones and grind flour. Take off your veil. Lift up your skirt and uncover your legs, and wade through the rivers.
Your nakedness will be uncovered, and your shame will be seen. I will take revenge, and I will spare no one."
Our Redeemer, whose name is the LORD of Armies, is the Holy One of Israel.
"Sit in silence and go into darkness, daughter of the Babylonians. You will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people. I let my own people be disgraced, and I handed them over to you. But you showed them no mercy. Even on the old you put a very heavy yoke.
You said, 'I will be queen forever!' But you did not think about these things or consider how they would end.
So now listen, you lover of pleasure, who sits safely and says to herself, 'I am the only one, and there is no one else. I will never be a widow or lose my children.'
Both of these things will come on you suddenly, in a single day: the loss of your children and becoming a widow. They will come on you in full, despite all your magic and all your powerful spells.
You have trusted in your wickedness and said, 'No one sees me.' Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray. You have said to yourself, 'I am the only one, and there is no one else.'
So disaster will come on you, and you will not know how to charm it away. Trouble will fall on you, and you will not be able to pay it off. Ruin you never expected will come on you suddenly.
Keep going, then, with your spells and your many magic tricks, which you have worked at since you were young. Maybe they will help you. Maybe you will scare someone.
All the advice you have received has only worn you out. Let your astrologers come forward, those who study the stars and make predictions month by month. Let them save you from what is coming on you.
Look, they are like straw. The fire will burn them up. They cannot even save themselves from the power of the flames. This is not a fire of coals to warm yourself, or a fire to sit beside.
That is all they can do for you, the ones you have worked with and traded with since you were young. Each of them will go their own way. There will be no one to save you."
